theory.question: What is three-step sparring?
theory.answer: A beginner's exercise for learning basics such as distance, facing, forearm conditioning, blocks, stances, counter-attacks and timing.

sparring: Three-step sparring (Sambo Matsoki) numbers 1-4. Attack: three middle-section front punches in walking stance, starting right leg back in low block. All defences start from parallel ready stance.
1: Right-leg-back walking stance, inner middle forearm block three times. Counter: reverse punch.

2: Left-leg-back L-stance, outer middle forearm block three times. Counter: advance left leg 45 degrees, bring right leg behind the opponent's front leg into left L-stance, right knifehand strike to the neck.
3: Left-leg-back L-stance, inward outer forearm block three times. Counter: slide forward into left L-stance, right front backfist to the face.
4: Left-leg-back L-stance, inward forearm block to the outside three times. Counter: move into sitting stance, focus with left hand, then double punch.

items: Named after patriot Ahn Chang-Ho (1876-1938). Starts in parallel ready stance; ends with right foot back to ready posture.

17-20: Same as 13-16, toward CF, kicking with left foot.
21-22: Rising forearm blocks, left then right.
23-24: Middle side knifehand strikes from sitting stance, left then right.

theory.question: What is 3 Step Semi-Free Sparring?
theory.answer: A step beyond basic 3 step sparring: three attacks in a row, three blocks or evasions, then a counter-attack.

sparring: Three-step sparring (Sambo Matsoki) numbers 8-10. Attack: three middle-section front punches in walking stance, starting right leg back in low block. Defences start from parallel ready stance.

8: Right L-stance, middle knifehand block to the inside twice. Counter: slide back at 45 degrees into right L-stance with forearm guarding block, right side kick landing in left L-stance, then right back fist or knifehand strike to the neck.

9: Right L-stance, middle palm push block to the outside three times. Counter: slide to the outside at 45 degrees into right L-stance with knifehand guarding block, right middle turning kick landing in vertical stance with knifehand strike to the neck.

10: Right L-stance, middle knifehand block to the inside twice. Counter: slide back at 45 degrees into right L-stance with knifehand guarding block, reverse side kick landing in right walking stance with left reverse knifehand strike to the philtrum.

Basic three-step semi-free sparring (Ban Jayoo Matsoki): attacker starts in L-stance with guarding block, either leg back; defender starts in parallel stance. Attack is back-leg-first kicking (front, side or turning kick); defence is any block suited to the kick; counter is a reverse punch.

theory.question: Meaning of Blue Belt
theory.answer: Blue stands for the heaven toward which a growing plant reaches, becoming a tall tree, as Tae Kwon-Do training advances.

theory.question: Two Step Sparring
theory.answer: A drill for intermediate students to learn more advanced techniques. Timing and distance match three step sparring, but the attacks are more varied, so the attacker can build different combinations.

sparring: TWO STEP SPARRING (IBO MATSOKI): Attacker starts right leg back, forearm guarding block. Defence starts in parallel ready stance.
1. Attack = High punch, front kick. Defence = Left leg back, walking stance, rising block; right leg back, walking stance, X fist pressing block. Counter = Twin vertical punch.

2. Attack = Side punch, fixed stance, turning kick. Defence = Right leg back, L stance, upward palm block; left leg back, L stance, waist block. Counter = Slide forward into right L stance, right side elbow.

3. Attack = Front kick, twin vertical punch. Defence = Right leg back, walking stance, X fist pressing block; left leg back, walking stance, outer forearm wedging block. Counter = Knee kick, at the same time pull opponent's shoulders.

4. Attack = Flat fingertip thrust, side kick. Defence = Right leg back, walking stance, knifehand rising block; left leg back, L stance, inward palm block. Counter = Front kick to coccyx, twin upset punch to kidneys.

THREE STEP SEMI-FREE SPARRING (BAN JAYOO MATSOKI), Intermediate Level: Attackers start in L stance, guarding block; defenders start in parallel stance. The attacker starts with either leg back every time.

Attack = Kicking with back leg first, any kick in any order from: front kick, side kick, turning kick, reverse side kick. Defence = Any block suitable for each individual kick. Counter = Any hand attack.

theory.question: What is Free Sparring
theory.answer: Free sparring means applying everything learned so far with no warning of the attack, so fewer defensive techniques can be rehearsed than in other sparring types. It can be done without pads and must be strictly non-contact. Semi-contact is allowed only with proper supervision (safety boots and gloves) from a qualified instructor.

sparring: TWO STEP SPARRING (IBO MATSOKI): Attacker starts right leg back, forearm guarding block. Defence starts in parallel ready stance.

5. Attack = Right back kick, left walking stance, high palm strike. Defence = Right L stance, palm waist block, left L stance, inward outer forearm block. Counter = Right walking stance, left reverse knifehand, middle inward strike (slipping right foot).

6. Attack = Right high turning kick, left walking stance arc-hand strike. Defence = Sitting stance twin straight forearm block (moving left foot diagonally), right L stance palm hooking block (grabbing the arm). Counter = Left side kick (still holding grabbed arm).

7. Attack = Right fixed stance, side fist side strike, left middle reverse turning kick. Defence = Left L stance, twin forearm block, right L stance knifehand guarding block (sliding away using block as guard only). Counter = Right high reverse turning kick.

8. Attack = Right middle side kick, right L stance, knifehand high strike (turning clockwise). Defence = Right L stance, inward inner forearm waist block, right L stance knifehand guarding block (double stepping). Counter = Left X stance, high backfist side strike.

THREE STEP SEMI-FREE SPARRING (BAN JAYOO MATSOKI), Advanced Level: Attackers start in L stance, guarding block; defenders start in parallel stance. The attacker starts with either leg back every time.
Attack = Stepping forward, execute any three techniques (hand or foot). Defence = Any block suitable for each individual technique. Counter = Any hand or foot technique.

practical.detail: Uses the existing 3 step counter attacks with additions, numbers 2 to 10 listed on the page (see sparring)

theory.question: Meaning of Red Belt
theory.answer: Red means danger: it tells the student to keep control and warns an opponent to keep away.

theory.question: What is One Step Sparring?
theory.answer: The most realistic form of sparring, since the defender cannot predict the attack, so quick reflexes are needed to defend and win. It differs from free sparring in that takedowns, arm locks and joint-breaking techniques are practised. Both students normally start in parallel stance, though the instructor may vary this.

sparring: ONE STEP SPARRING (ILBO MATSOKI): Use the existing 3 step counter attacks with additions, as listed below. Both attacker and defender start in parallel ready position; attacker steps forward with right leg into walking stance and punches with right hand. On the second occasion the same attacker steps forward with left leg and left hand punching. (Only right hand side is shown.)

2. Move the left leg forward 45 degrees, move the right leg behind the opponent's front leg into a left 'L' stance, execute a right knifehand strike to the neck, followed by side kick with right foot and step away.
3. In a left 'L' stance execute a right front backfist strike to the face followed by an upward punch (left hand) and hooking punch (right hand).
4. Move the left leg into a sitting stance, focus with left hand, execute double punch, followed by turning kick with right leg followed by reverse side kick with the left leg.

5. Move to the right into sitting stance parallel to opponent. Execute a left outer forearm block and a high section punch simultaneously, grab head with both hands and pull down whilst performing a left knee strike.
6. Move to the right, form a sitting stance parallel to opponent, execute left outer knifehand guard and a high inward knifehand strike to the neck, followed by upper elbow strike with left elbow.

7. Move right foot to left foot, pushing off left foot slide back at a 45 degree angle into a right 'L' stance with a forearm guarding block, execute a right front kick landing in a right walking stance double punch, reaching under their punching arm perform a hooking block to the top (right hand), brace elbow with left hand and take forward into arm lock.

8. Move right foot to left foot, pushing off left foot slide back at a 45 degree angle into a right 'L' stance with a forearm guarding block. Execute a right side kick landing in left 'L' stance, right front back fist strike or knifehand strike to the neck, grab their punching hand with your left hand, pull in and elbow strike to their head with your right arm whilst sliding into vertical stance.

9. Slide back at a 45 degree angle to the outside of your opponent into a right 'L' stance with a knifehand guarding block. Execute a right mid section turning kick, put the kicking foot behind the opponent's front foot landing in vertical stance while executing a knifehand strike to the neck, step through, put your right arm under their punching arm and using your inner forearm to their main neck artery (carotid artery), grab your inner forearm with your other hand and squeeze.

10. Move right foot to left foot pushing off left foot, slide back at a 45 degree angle into a right 'L' stance with a knifehand guarding block. Execute a reverse side kick, land in a right walking stance whilst executing a left hand reverse knifehand strike to the philtrum, step out perform turning kick with your left leg, step down reverse turning kick with your right leg. (attacker performs checking block).
THREE STEP SEMI-FREE SPARRING (advanced) and Free Sparring are listed in practical; no further detail on this page.

Includes pushing and pressing palm blocks, forearm and knife-hand blocks, back piercing kicks, elbow thrusts, hooking kicks, cross cuts, jump X-stances. Ends with return to ready stance.

general.title: What is Tae Kwon-Do
general.summary: Tae Kwon-Do is a Korean unarmed combat art for self-defence that also serves as a disciplined way of life.

items.title: The name
items.text: The name joins words for jumping and kicking with the foot, striking or smashing with the hand, and the idea of a way or art.

items.title: Self-defence
items.text: Students learn to defend through strikes, kicks, blocks, evasion and interception.

items.title: Way of life
items.text: It is also a discipline that shapes character, and used carelessly it can be dangerous.

general.title: History
general.summary: The art grew out of older Oriental fighting traditions and was refined into its modern form in Korea.

items.text: The source page gives only a brief overview: Tae Kwon-Do descends from ancient Oriental combat methods and was perfected in Korea.

general.title: The Tenets
general.summary: Five guiding principles that every student works to live by, in and out of the dojang.

items.title: Courtesy
items.text: Be polite and respectful to instructors, seniors and fellow students.

items.title: Integrity
items.text: Be honest with yourself and know right from wrong.

items.title: Perseverance
items.text: Keep working towards a goal, whether a new grade or a technique.

items.title: Self Control
items.text: Stay calm and never lose your temper; train within your own ability.

items.title: Indomitable Spirit
items.text: Show courage and stand by your principles even against overwhelming odds.

general.title: Student Oath
general.summary: Five promises each student makes about conduct and the responsible use of the art.

items.text: I will follow the rules and regulations of the Association.
I will work to remain modest.
I will be courteous and respectful to all members, especially seniors.
I will use the art only to defend myself or to protect those who cannot.
I will never misuse what I have learned.

general.title: Conduct in the Dojang
general.summary: A set of bows and greetings marks arriving, training and leaving.

items.text: Bow as you enter the dojang.
Bow to the instructor from a respectful distance.
Greet your fellow students.
Bow to the instructor when lining up at the start of class.
Bow to the instructor when lining up at the end of class.
Bow again as you leave.

general.title: Being a Good Student
general.summary: Ten points on attitude, loyalty, example and reliability.

items.text: Stay keen to learn and ask questions; you can learn anywhere.
Give more than your fees: help with demonstrations, teaching and dojang tasks.
Set a good example for lower grades.
Be loyal and do not criticise your instructor, the art or its teaching methods.
Practise and try to apply what your instructor teaches.
Remember your behaviour outside the dojang reflects on the art and your instructor.
If your instructor disapproves of a technique learned elsewhere, drop it or train where you learned it.
Never be disrespectful; if you disagree, follow the instruction first and discuss it afterwards.
Arrive early and attend regularly.
Never betray a trust.

general.title: Rules & Regulations
general.summary: Fifteen practical rules covering membership, fees, dress, behaviour and grading.

items.text: Complete and sign the required forms before you begin training.
Obtain TAGB membership and a record card after your first four weeks.
Pay fees in the first week of each month; late payment carries a penalty.
Do not let fee arrears build up.
Give one month's notice to adjust fees for breaks such as holidays.
If you miss lessons and fees for two months or more, pay a re-enrolment fee before returning.
No smoking, eating, drinking or jewellery in the dojang.
Never smoke while wearing a dobok.
Take your belt off when eating or drinking in your dobok.
After your first grading, train in a dobok unless the instructor allows tracksuit or street clothes.
The most senior student present starts training until the instructor arrives.
Misusing the art leads to disciplinary action.
Grading depends on attendance, the instructor's judgement and technical ability.
To change schools you need a transfer form and prior permission from both instructors.
Own a Students Handbook after your first grading.

general.title: Why Patterns (Tul)
general.summary: Patterns are set sequences of attacks and defences against imaginary opponents, used to measure progress and sharpen technique.

items.title: What a pattern is
items.text: A fixed series of mostly defensive and offensive movements performed against one or more imaginary opponents; it shows a student's progress and skill.

items.title: Benefits
items.text: Patterns refine technique, help sparring, improve flexibility and freedom of movement, teach body shifting, build muscle, balance and breath control, and teach things other training does not.

items.title: Why twenty-four
items.text: General Choi Hong Hi compared a human life to one day; the twenty-four patterns stand for the twenty-four hours of a day, or his whole life, and a lasting legacy for mankind.

items.title: Performing patterns
items.text: Start and finish on the same spot; keep correct posture and facing; tense and relax at the right moments; move rhythmically without stiffness; follow the speed changes; perfect each pattern before the next; understand each movement's purpose; make every movement realistic.
